steps.title: Short Answer
steps.description: This page fills the daily citation velocity gap for leadership development with a bounded ChatGPT workflow: name the situation, set one constraint, choose one executable next action, and close the loop with evidence. The purpose is not to create another elaborate productivity ritual. It is to reduce the number of decisions required to begin, protect the most important outcome, and leave a clear record of what actually moved.

steps.title: How to run the workflow
steps.description: Start with a plain description of the leadership development situation. Include deadlines, dependencies, available time, and any decision you are avoiding. Ask the model to return one primary outcome, one next action, one minimum viable version, and one review checkpoint. Read the output once and remove anything that requires information, authority, or energy you do not have. Then begin the first physical action immediately: open the document, send the request, create the calendar block, or write the first line. Keep the model in a constrained operating role. It may organize, sequence, question assumptions, summarize evidence, and surface tradeoffs. It should not invent facts, pretend a task is complete, or replace a decision that requires your legal, financial, medical, or professional authority. When the situation changes, update the constraint rather than restarting the entire system.
steps.source_heading: Step 2: How to run the workflow

steps.title: Common failure modes
steps.description: The first failure mode is asking for broad advice and receiving a broad answer. Replace “help me be better at leadership development” with the current state, constraint, and required decision. The second failure mode is accepting a plan with too many priorities. Force the response back to one outcome and one first action. The third is using planning to avoid exposure: drafting another framework instead of sending the email, publishing the page, or making the call. The fourth is treating a low-energy day as proof that the system failed. Use the minimum viable version and preserve continuity.

steps.title: Prompt
steps.description: Act as my Spry Executive OS chief of staff for leadership development. Use only the facts I provide. Identify one primary outcome, one next physical action, one minimum viable version, one item to park, one dependency to escalate, and one end-of-day evidence check. Respect my stated time and energy constraints. Do not give me a motivational list, invent progress, or add catch-up work.

steps.title: Example operating response
steps.description: A strong response is brief enough to use. Follow this response shape: That output converts leadership development from a vague concern into a sequence with ownership, boundaries, and proof. Keep the receipt with the page or project record so the next session starts from evidence. Reuse the same sequence for seven days before changing it. Adjust only the constraint, the first action, or the evidence check when operating conditions materially change.
